operations.name: parseSelectors(reference)
operations.asserts: the grammar rows: canonical spelling and the thrown message

operations.name: scan(source, lexer?)
operations.asserts: the mask and shape rows: the lexical invariants

operations.name: planSection(source, reference, lexer?)
operations.asserts: the resolution rows: text, startLine, endLine, ranges, kind, error

operations.name: diagnose(source, reference, lexer?)
operations.returns: { status, plan, firstLine, error, code, selector, scope, candidates, advice }
operations.asserts: never throws; status is ok | failed | invalid, and the failure carries the fields below. Implemented in the JavaScript reference; not required of a port until band rows land — a port that omits it still passes every corpus row

error_codes.comment: Stable codes, asserted in test.mjs and read by a host choosing a band. A code is added, never renamed; a message may be reworded without breaking a caller.
error_codes.grammar: The reference is malformed as written and no file was read. Thrown as SectionReferenceError.
error_codes.resolution: The reference is well formed and the file cannot answer it. Thrown as a plain Error.

layers.name: grammar
layers.selector: rows with input === null (they consult no file)

layers.name: mask
asserts: mask() output for one lexer entry
mask length and newline offsets are preserved
needs: a lexer table for the language

layers.name: shapes
asserts: declarations(maskedLine): kind, name, headerFrom, body, end, line

layers.name: blocks
asserts: the block tree: nesting, anchors, regions, conditions, Allman / indented / arrow bodies

layers.name: resolution
layers.selector: rows with input !== null (they name a fixture)

layers.name: documents
asserts: markers, gitignore, --lenient, region directives, the JSON/TOML/INI/YAML rules, round trips

layers.name: differential
layers.selector: two implementations, over the corpus plus generated cases

layers.name: profile
asserts: the editor's landing line and cause
the band the gate refuses, and that it refuses every one of them
every failing reference in one document pass
layers.optional: Only an implementation that offers a profile is held to this layer. A port that implements the resolver alone skips it — RFC 1 §6.3 — and this is the one layer a port may pass by not having it.

row_fields.name: unique; `<category>:<case>` for parse rows, a slug for resolution rows
row_fields.mode: not a row field — the generator uses it to declare a case; a written row distinguishes the two kinds by `input`
row_fields.input: fixture path, relative to the repository root; null for a parse row
row_fields.reference: the section reference under test, without the leading `#`
row_fields.text: the exact selection text, or null when the row expects an error
row_fields.ranges: [[from, to], ...] — the spread of text as 1-based inclusive line pairs
row_fields.kind: region | declaration | property | condition | anchor | lines | multiple; null for a parse row
row_fields.error: the exact thrown message, or null
row_fields.errorCode: the stable code of the failure (RFC 1 §3.6): `grammar/*` when no file was consulted, `resolution/*` when the file cannot answer. Proposed, not yet a row field: the codes exist on every thrown failure and are asserted in test.mjs, and a row gains the field when band rows land

masks[].name: the lexer entry
masks[].mask: the exact masked text: same length, every newline at its own offset

shapes[].name: the spelling under test
shapes[].path: a file name, to select the lexer
shapes[].line: the **raw** line handed to declarations(), not a masked one
shapes[].declared: the expected entries, field by field

corpora.optional: A port that implements no profile does not read this file; a port that offers one must reproduce every row. It is the only corpus a port may pass by not having the feature.

resolutions[].name: `<target>:<reference>`
resolutions[].file: the jump fixture the reference resolves against, under `test/fixtures/jump`
resolutions[].reference: the `#` fragment content, without the leading `#`
resolutions[].editor: { firstLine, cause } — where `jump/editor` lands and how it got there
resolutions[].gate: the code `jump/gate` fails with, or null when the gate resolves it too
resolutions[].note: authored, and not always present: why the row exists

documents[].name: the document, without its extension
documents[].document: the Markdown text, embedded so a consumer needs no disk
documents[].files: `[[path, text], …]` — every file the markers name, embedded
documents[].outcome: { passed, checked, failures[] } — each failure naming its `reference`, `code` and `selector`

obligations.assert_every_row: Fail when a corpus row is unaccounted for. Skipping a row is how a port passes while being wrong.
obligations.read_from_repo: Read the corpora from the repository; do not copy them into the port, so a corpus change reaches every port at once.
obligations.never_hand_edit: The corpora are generated from the reference implementation. Regenerate, never edit.
obligations.hand_check_changes: A changed row is reviewed, not trusted: a consistently wrong implementation bakes its own bug into the contract.
obligations.error_rows_matter: The rows expecting an error are what catch an over-eager matcher.
obligations.discriminate: Every row must be one whose wrong answer looks different from its right answer.
